facts.statement: Liaoningornis is a genus of bird from the Lower Cretaceous of China.
facts.quote: Liaoningornis (meaning "bird of Liaoning" in Greek) is a genus of bird from Lower Cretaceous China.

facts.statement: The genus was described by Linhai Hou in 1996 and 1997.
facts.quote: It was described by Linhai Hou in 1996 and 1997.

facts.statement: The only known species is Liaoningornis longidigitus.
facts.quote: The only known species is Liaoningornis longidigitris.

facts.statement: While Zhou and Hou (2002) considered Liaoningornis the oldest known member of the Ornithurae, a 2012 re-analysis by Jingmai O'Connor identified it as an enantiornithean similar to Eoalulavis.
facts.quote: Zhou and Hou in 2002 considered Liaoningornis to be the oldest known member of the Ornithurae. However, a 2012 re-analysis by Jingmai O'Connor showed that it was in fact an enantiornithean similar to Eoalulavis.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Liaoningornis is classified within the parent group Ornithuromorpha.

rejected.statement: The single known fossil is an incomplete semi-articulated skeleton the size of a sparrow.
rejected.quote: The single fossil is an incomplete semi-articulated skeleton the size of a sparrow.
